evidence.observation: R0.4 reads: 'An element the root owns, a constraint the root attaches to an included fact type included, is checked by U1–U8 exactly as today.' The phrase 'an included fact type included' is garbled (a duplicated word), and the parenthetical apposition makes the binding rule ambiguous to parse. The intended meaning — root-owned constraints attached to included fact types are checked exactly as today — is recoverable from section 2 VG3 ('An element the root owns is checked as today (R0.4)') and VG3-C3, but R0.4 is a binding rule and should read unambiguously.

concerns.recommendation: Rewrite R0.4's second sentence, e.g. 'An element the root owns — including a constraint the root attaches to an included fact type — is checked by U1–U8 exactly as today.'
concerns.title: Garbled wording in binding rule R0.4

summary: Plan r1 reviewed against the repository at this checkout. The sha256 of the plan file matches the request. All test files named in the section 9 lanes and helpers (tests/test_mc1_model_includes.py:write_case) exist; the five new test files are correctly absent. The binding rules (R0.1-R0.7), decisions D1-D12 and section 6 controls are mutually consistent: D3(a)'s include exemption keeps R0.4/R0.5 for root-owned elements across U1-U8 (VG3-C2/C3), D4(a)'s U1 relaxation is guarded by U4/U5/U7 span checks and VG4-C3 in both directions, D2(a)'s D-12 widening is fenced by VG2-C2's four refusal cases, and VG4 is genuinely a pin of existing include-root evolve behaviour (service.py:261-276 composition, :1610-1613 ownership enforcement, contract 'Shared vocabulary evolution' 618-664) plus D4 and D6, not unstated new work. VG1's machine-speed dependence is addressed by the call-count guard (spec T9) and prototype-derived bounds. Three concerns: the plan covers the D3(b) fallback but not the D2(b) fallback that VG5's sample-constraint round presupposes, and two low-severity citation/editorial slips.
